title: Statement
logline: Days after the godown, at the bail hearing, Bhaiyaji's lawyer offers Nandini a free lie: say she did not send the fake inspector in, and Nirala falls alone while she walks. She says she sent him, and says why that truth is what makes the recording evidence. Bhaiyaji and Tripathi are charged and refused bail; on her own statement she is suspended and will stand trial beside Nirala, who gets bail. Weeks later the old talkies is a help desk, and the two of them have the same court date next month.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut; names, 'ji', 'sahab', 'madam', 'thana', 'godown', 'FIR' and 'SI' kept as spoken in India.

characters.name: Nandini Joshi
characters.role: LEAD. Sub-Inspector, Imlipur thana. In b1 to b10 she is the prosecution's witness at the bail hearing, days after the godown night; in b11, weeks later, she is suspended and out of uniform.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall (about 170 cm), lean, very straight-backed, long neck. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, level dark-brown eyes, a firm mouth that rarely smiles. Black hair, clean centre parting, low ponytail to the shoulder blades; no fringe, no loose strands. No make-up, no bindi, no jewellery, no watch. PERIOD 1 (b1 to b10): approved force uniform, crisp: sandy khaki shirt with two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves buttoned at the wrist; dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars each; white lantern on a round teal patch on each upper sleeve; khaki trousers; black belt with a black handcuff pouch on her right hip; black shoes; blue ballpoint pen clipped in her left chest pocket. No cap, no name tag, no stars, no helmet. From b9 (after the epaulettes come off) her shoulder straps are bare khaki. PERIOD 2 (b11 only): a plain mustard-yellow cotton kurta with elbow-length sleeves over off-white trousers, the same low ponytail, the same blue pen tucked behind her right ear.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Indian English with a neutral, educated small-city north-Indian accent; no British or American colour. Keeps 'ji', 'madam', 'SI', 'thana'. Quick and clipped. Under pressure she gets quieter, slower and more exact, never louder. Dry, not sarcastic. In court every line is low, clear and exact: l07 is three short sentences with a full stop between each; l10 is crisper, not louder (if casting shows [sharply] raising her volume, S10 swaps it to [flatly]). l11 lands its weight on the last word, 'is'. In b11 the dryness has warmth under it, still no smile in the voice.

characters.name: Sudhir Nirala
characters.role: The former 'Inspector' of the fake thana, now an accused in the dock. Gets bail in b8. In b11 he works the help desk beside Nandini.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short (about 160 cm), narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, a neat black pencil moustache, clean-shaven chin. PERIOD 2, all episode: NO CAP for the first time in the series (his peaked cap lies on the evidence table in court): flat, neatly side-parted black hair pressed down by years under a cap. A plain white half-sleeve shirt and grey trousers, no medal, no holster, no belt tail. Same outfit in court and in b11 (writer's call to keep to one second-period drawing; S6 may differ if the bible's look is read otherwise).
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, forty, light careful tenor. Careful, slightly old-fashioned small-town north-Indian English, as learnt from manuals: full forms, no contractions ('did not', 'It is', 'would have been'), every English word pronounced with great care; no British or American colour. Addresses the bench as 'Your Honour'. Unhurried, courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes. Under pressure he becomes more formal and quieter. In b3 he is desperate but still formal: thin, steady, fast, not loud. l14 is said as a plain fact, with pride he does not show. In b11 he is calm, almost light.

characters.name: Pushpa Kumari
characters.role: Head Constable at the Imlipur thana. Sits alone in the public seats in b4; brings the suspension order in b9 and is left with the thana and the thirty complaints.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short (about 152 cm) and solid, round shoulders. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low on her nose. Grey-streaked black hair in a tight high bun with TWO STEEL KNITTING NEEDLES pushed through it in a cross. Approved force uniform with ONE off-white bar on each teal epaulette, lantern sleeve patches, under an open hand-knitted plum-purple cardigan with two sagging pockets, a ball of orange wool in the right pocket. In b4 a second pair of needles and a half-knitted piece lie still in her lap. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Plain, unhurried small-town north-Indian English with a clear Hindi accent; short sentences; keeps 'madam' and 'DSP sahab'. No British or American colour. Says the important thing in the fewest words. Never surprised. Warmth shows only as dryness: l20 is a promise said like a duty roster.

characters.name: Balram 'Bhaiyaji' Thakur
characters.role: Accused, on the bench for the accused. Silent in this episode: seen in b2, b6 and b8.
characters.look: Indian man, 45, broad and solid, about 178 cm, thick neck, big square hands. Brown skin, thick black hair combed straight back, a full black moustache, an unhurried closed-lip smile that is his resting face (gone from b6 on). A spotless white cotton kurta with the sleeves pushed up his forearms over white pyjama trousers; brown leather sandals. A heavy gold watch on his LEFT wrist. His dark sunglasses are FOLDED IN HIS RIGHT HAND all episode, never on his head or eyes. No key ring: his right index finger is bare. No religious marks, no party colours, no scarf.
characters.voice_note: Silent in this episode. No lines.

characters.name: Dayashankar Tripathi
characters.role: Accused, beside Bhaiyaji on the bench. Silent in this episode: seen in b2 and b8.
characters.look: Indian man, 56, large, heavy and slow, about 175 cm, a big soft belly straining his shirt. Warm-brown skin, bald dome with a fringe of grey hair at the sides, heavy jowls, clean-shaven, half-closed sleepy eyes. Approved force uniform worn slack: khaki half-sleeve shirt with the top two buttons open over a white vest, teal epaulettes with three off-white bars, lantern sleeve patches, khaki trousers. A red-and-white checked gamchha over his LEFT shoulder. FOR ONCE NO PEANUTS: both hands empty in his lap, no shells anywhere. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Silent in this episode. No lines.

characters.name: Magistrate (unnamed)
characters.role: Presides over the bail hearing. Voice only; shown as hands on the desk, a pen, a file, the hand bell. Never a face, never above the wrists. Age is a casting guide only.
characters.look: Never a face. Two older hands, plain cuffs of a dark sleeve, no rings: on a raised wooden desk with a file, a pen stand and a brass hand bell; in b7 and b8 reaching to the evidence table.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female (cast as Mitali in content/series2/cast.json), older, level, unhurried, formal. The formal Indian English of the bench, neutral north-Indian accent, no British or American colour. Never raises the voice and never sounds surprised; every name in l15 to l17 read clearly, with Indian pronunciation (BUL-raam THAA-koor, da-yaa-SHUN-kar tri-PAA-thi, su-DHEER ni-RAA-laa, nun-DI-ni JO-shi). l13 is a dry question, not incredulous.

characters.name: Defence lawyer
characters.role: Bhaiyaji's counsel ('my client'). Voice only; shown as a black-coated back and a hand holding a pen. Never a face. Age is a casting guide only.
characters.look: Never a face. A black advocate's coat seen from behind, white collar bands just showing at the neck, one hand raised holding a black fountain pen.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, smooth, amused, quick (cast as Ketan M in content/series2/cast.json). Fluent urban courtroom Indian English, no British or American colour. Courteous; he enjoys the trap and never laughs outright. Must differ from Bhaiyaji by pace: quick against unhurried. l08 is cut off by Nandini on 'that'.

location: magistrate_room (b1 to b10): a small court room. A raised wooden desk with a file, a pen stand and a brass hand bell; the magistrate is hands only. A wooden witness stand with a rail to one side, where Nandini stands; a dock rail opposite, where Nirala stands. In front of the desk the EVIDENCE TABLE: twenty-four sealed brown envelopes with red wax in rows, the peaked cap, the brass medal, the wooden revolver lying on its side, and Pushpa's keypad phone in its knitted orange cover. A bench for the accused. Public seats, empty except for Pushpa. High windows, flat daylight. No flags, no emblems, no portraits, no crowd. talkies_lobby (b11): the lobby of the old Roopam Talkies in morning light, with a new hand-painted board over the desk (painted blank; overlay ov_helpdesk_board) and no marks of rank anywhere.
time_of_day: b1 to b10: some days after the godown night, a weekday, flat daylight from high windows; b9 and b10 are a little later, after the hearing has risen. b11: some weeks later, morning light. Clocks in frame, if any, have hands and no numerals.

beats.action: OPEN INSIDE THE QUESTION, no establishing shot. Shot 1 (over the shoulder, close): a black-coated back fills picture-right, one hand raised holding a pen towards the witness stand; beyond it Nandini in the stand, in uniform, both hands on the rail, face to camera. 0.5 s of room tone, then l01 plays here. Shot 2 (insert, top-down), on the last words of l01: the evidence table: twenty-four sealed brown envelopes in rows, red wax on each, the peaked cap, the brass medal on its striped ribbon, the wooden revolver lying on its side, Pushpa's keypad phone in its knitted orange cover.

lines.speaker: defence_lawyer
lines.text: [smoothly] SI Joshi. Yes or no. Did you send this man into the godown?

beats.action: The lawyer lays out both answers for her, pleasantly, his pen tapping the rail of the stand. Shot 1 (single): Nirala at the dock rail, bare-headed for the first time in the series, flat side-parted hair, white half-sleeve shirt, hands at his sides: l02 up to 'on his own' plays over him. Shot 2 (two-shot): the accused bench: Bhaiyaji in his white kurta, calm, sunglasses folded in his right hand; Tripathi beside him, gamchha on his left shoulder, hands empty, no peanuts: the rest of l02 ('his gang, my client the victim') plays here. Shot 3 (single, close): Nandini in the stand, unmoving: l03 up to its ellipsis ('Say 'yes'...'). Shot 4 (insert): Nirala's peaked cap on the evidence table: the rest of l03 ('and you sent a fake policeman in, against your own DSP's order').

lines.speaker: defence_lawyer
lines.text: [smoothly] Say 'no', and an impostor went into that godown on his own: his gang, my client the victim.

lines.speaker: defence_lawyer
lines.text: [amused] Say 'yes'... and you sent a fake policeman in, against your own DSP's order.

beats.action: Nirala cannot bear it. Shot 1 (single): he grips the dock rail with both hands and leans forward, formal even now: l04, cut off on the dash. Shot 2 (insert), in the 0.5 s after the cut-off: the magistrate's hand comes down flat on the brass hand bell. Shot 3 (insert): the magistrate's two hands on the desk, the pen laid across the file: l05 plays over the hands. The magistrate is never seen above the wrists.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] Your Honour, madam did not send me. I went alone—

lines.speaker: magistrate
lines.text: [calm] You will keep quiet. The question is for the witness.

beats.action: THE HELD BEAT, no dialogue, 3.5 s. Everyone in the room has offered her the safe answer. Shot 1 (single, 1.5 s): Nandini in the stand, eyes down, her right hand on the rail; beside her hand on the rail, the folded carbon copy of her seizure memo. Shot 2 (wide on the public seats, otherwise empty, 1.0 s): Pushpa alone on the front bench, the knitting still in her lap, needles stopped. Shot 3 (insert, 1.0 s): the brass medal on the evidence table, among the sealed envelopes.

Shot 1 (wide two-shot from behind the magistrate's desk, 0.5 s before l06): the stand picture-left, the dock picture-right, the length of the room between them; Nandini has turned her head to the dock. Nirala's hands lie slack on the dock rail. l06 plays here. Shot 2 (single, front on): she faces the desk and answers, low, clear, exact: l07.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] Nirala ji. The statement is mine.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] I sent him. The phone was mine. So was the decision.

beats.action: She goes on before the lawyer can enjoy it. Shot 1 (over the shoulder, as b1): the lawyer's pen raised, her face sharp beyond it: l08, cut off by Nandini, and l09 play over this one frame. Shot 2 (Nandini single, front on): l10. Shot 3 (insert): the lawyer's pen, stopped against the rail of the stand: l11. Shot 4 (insert): Pushpa's keypad phone in its knitted orange cover on the evidence table: l12 from 'In Bhaiyaji's voice:' up to 'Inspector!'. Shot 5 (insert): Bhaiyaji's right hand closed hard on his folded sunglasses: the rest of l12 ('It's you I was waiting for.').

lines.speaker: defence_lawyer
lines.text: [amused] So you admit that—

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Yes. Which is why that recording is mine.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] A phone found in an impostor's pocket is not evidence.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] A phone sent in by an SI is.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] In Bhaiyaji's voice: 'Fake Inspector! It's you I was waiting for.'

beats.action: Shot 1 (insert, 1.0 s before l13 and through it): the magistrate's hand reaches to the evidence table, lifts one sealed envelope from the rows and turns it over: the red wax unbroken. Shot 2 (single): Nirala in the dock, straight-backed, answering as he answered Nandini in s2e02: l14.

lines.speaker: magistrate
lines.text: [calm] Twenty-four envelopes. Not one of them opened?

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] It is case property, Your Honour.

beats.action: The order, in the magistrate's voice, over the faces in turn. Shot 1 (insert, in the 1.0 s silence): the envelope back in its row; the magistrate's hand resting on the brass medal at the corner of the table, clear of the sealed exhibits (the slide is sound only). Shot 2 (single): Bhaiyaji on the bench, the smile gone, sunglasses folded in his fist: 'Balram Thakur,' of l15. Shot 3 (single): Tripathi beside him, hands empty in his lap: the rest of l15. Shot 4 (single): Nirala in the dock: l16. Shot 5 (wide two-shot from behind the magistrate's desk, as b5): Nandini in the stand picture-left, Nirala in the dock picture-right, one frame: 'And SI Nandini Joshi:' of l17. Shot 6 (Nandini single, close, front on; S4 may reuse the b5 shot 2 framing): the rest of l17.

lines.speaker: magistrate
lines.text: [calm] Balram Thakur, Dayashankar Tripathi: charges framed, bail rejected.

lines.speaker: magistrate
lines.text: [calm] Sudhir Nirala: bail granted.

lines.speaker: magistrate
lines.text: [calm] And SI Nandini Joshi: on your own statement, you will stand trial as well.

beats.action: The room emptying: a cut in time. The accused bench and the dock are empty; the evidence table is still in place. Shot 1 (two-shot at the witness stand): Pushpa comes to the stand with a long brown office envelope, open, no wax (unlike the exhibits), and holds it up: l18. Shot 2 (insert, in the 1.2 s silence): Nandini's fingers slide one two-bar teal epaulette off her shoulder strap; the second is already in her other hand. Shot 3 (insert): the two epaulettes laid in Pushpa's open palm: l19. Shot 4 (two-shot): Pushpa tucks them into her cardigan pocket beside the orange wool: l20.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [quietly] Suspension order, madam. DSP sahab has signed it.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Keep them safe, Pushpa ji.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [deadpan] I'll write all thirty FIRs, madam.

beats.action: Shot 1 (single, from Nandini's side): Nirala, bare-headed, at her elbow by the stand: l21. Shot 2 (single): Nandini, bare khaki shoulder straps where the bars were: l22, his own rule given back. Shot 3 (two-shot from low behind the evidence table, held 1.0 s after l22): the brass medal sharp in the foreground at the corner where the magistrate left it; behind it, Nandini and Nirala side by side, both looking down at it. Neither moves to touch it.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] Madam... if you had lied, you would have been safe.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] You taught me yourself: whatever you write, say it aloud.

beats.action: FINAL IMAGE, resolution, weeks later. Shot 1 (wide, 1.5 s before l23): the talkies lobby in morning light from the high windows, the new hand-painted board over the desk (painted blank; overlay ov_helpdesk_board), no marks of rank anywhere; the ticket-booth grille stands open and empty. Shot 2 (two-shot at the desk): Nandini seated in a plain mustard kurta, pen behind her right ear, the brass medal lying on a stack of forms as a paperweight; Nirala standing beside her in his white half-sleeve shirt, no cap, a string of blank grey cardboard tokens in his hand: l23. Shot 3 (single): Nirala standing, the token string held up in his hand: l24. Shot 4 (single): Nandini, eyes up to him, chin turned a fraction towards the complainants' bench: l25. Shot 5 (single, held 1.2 s after l26): Nirala turns to the bench, where one pair of hands waits in a lap at the edge of frame (never a face), and lifts the first token off the string (overlay ov_token_1): l26.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] This is a help desk, not a thana, madam.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] My court date is next month. Yours?

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Same day. Call them in.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Next! Token one.

sfx_notes: Bed, b1 to b10, loopable (one magistrate_room ambience): a large quiet room with hard walls, a slow ceiling fan, faint birds and traffic far off through high windows. Nothing in it is loud.
b1: room tone only for 0.5 s, then l01. A dry pen tap on wood once under 'Yes or no'.
b2: the pen tapping the rail of the stand, light and regular, under l02 and l03; it stops at the end of l03.
b3: l04 is cut off by one sharp ring of a brass hand bell; the ring decays fully during the 0.5 s silence and is gone before l05 starts.
b4: 3.5 s of near-silence: fan, one creak of the wooden stand. No music sting.

b6: the bed ducks under l12 so every word of the quote is clear; a small leather creak of Bhaiyaji's grip on the sunglasses after its last word. No phone filter: she is quoting, not playing the recording.
b7: paper and wax: the soft scrape of a sealed envelope lifted and turned.
b8: in the 1.0 s silence, the dry slide of a ribbon and a metal disc across wood. Under l15 to l17 nothing else.
b9: the room has emptied: the bed thins, footsteps on a wooden floor fading off, a door far off. In the 1.2 s silence the faint click of a shoulder-strap button and the soft drag of cloth.

b11: new bed: talkies lobby by morning: birds through the high windows, a far goods-train horn once in the 1.5 s opening wide, the light rattle of cardboard tokens on string. The bed ducks under l26 and it stays fully clear; then 1.2 s of lobby tone to the end.
music_note: No music in b1 to b5: the court is room tone and the pen. A single low sustained string note enters under b6 at l10, ducks right down under l12, and holds thinly under b8's order. It drops out for b9. In b10 a soft warm chord enters under the held two-shot over the medal and carries across the cut into b11's morning; it lifts slightly on 'Call them in' (l25), ducks under l26, and resolves on the final hold. Instrumental, no melody hook, no percussion hits.
ending_question: Resolved. What is still open is said in the last lines: next month, on the same day, both of them stand trial, and without a uniform the first token has already been called. Was the truth worth this price?
writer_notes: S5 English adaptation of script.hi.json, not a literal translation. Same beats, same line ids (l01 to l26), same speakers, same order, same silent_seconds per beat, same tags in the same positions. Only text, target_seconds, the cue words quoted in action, sfx_notes and music_note, and the English fields (title, names, voice notes, language, ending_question) differ. Picture, props, sound effects and music are shared with the Hindi cut.

Action fields: identical to the Hindi script except that each quoted Hindi cue word is replaced by the English words where the same shot change falls: b2 ('on his own', 'his gang, my client the victim', 'Say 'yes'...', 'and you sent a fake policeman in, against your own DSP's order'), b6 ('In Bhaiyaji's voice:' up to 'Inspector!', 'It's you I was waiting for.'), b8 ('Balram Thakur,', 'And SI Nandini Joshi:'). sfx b1 cue is 'Yes or no'; the music lift in b11 is on 'Call them in'.

Register replaces the Hindi registers: the lawyer quick and fluent, the magistrate formal ('You will keep quiet', 'charges framed, bail rejected', 'bail granted' are the bench's Indian English), Nirala in full forms without contractions ('did not', 'It is', 'would have been') and 'Your Honour' for 'हुज़ूर', which an English voice is likely to misread. Nandini dry and clipped. Pushpa plain and short; her one contraction ('I'll') keeps l20 a duty-roster line rather than a vow.

Kept as said in India: 'SI', 'ji', 'madam', 'DSP sahab', 'thana', 'godown', 'FIR', 'Bhaiyaji'. 'Fake Inspector' for 'नक़ली Inspector'. Pronunciation dictionary candidates for the English voices: Joshi (JO-shi), Nirala (ni-RAA-laa), Bhaiyaji (BHAI-yaa-ji), Balram Thakur (BUL-raam THAA-koor), Dayashankar Tripathi (da-yaa-SHUN-kar tri-PAA-thi), Sudhir (su-DHEER), Pushpa (PUSH-paa), sahab (SAA-hab), thana (THAA-naa), godown (GO-down). The magistrate's English casting pass read the names clearly (cast.json), but that was a Hindi line.

The third test (bible critic_focus) is carried in speech by l09 to l11: 'Which is why that recording is mine. A phone found in an impostor's pocket is not evidence. A phone sent in by an SI is.' 'found' is the bible's own word for the impostor's phone. l11 ends on a stressed 'is'; if the voice drops it so the line sounds unfinished, S10 retakes, and the fallback text is 'One sent in by an SI is evidence.' (a text change: it needs the subtitle to follow).

l03 says 'against your own DSP's order' where the Hindi says 'order के ख़िलाफ़'. The bible reveal for b2 names whose order it was; the English needs the possessive to sound natural, and it is not new matter. l12 now quotes the English recording word for word: s2b01 script.en.json b10 has '[laughs] Fake Inspector! Aaiye... it's you I was waiting for.', and l12 says 'Fake Inspector! It's you I was waiting for.', dropping 'Aaiye...' exactly as the Hindi l12 drops 'आइए...' (bible s2b03 b6: she quotes only what is on the recording). If s2b01 en b10 changes in its own review, l12 follows it word for word. Likewise l22 renders the s2e02 b4 rule 'जो लिखो, बोलकर लिखो' as 'whatever you write, say it aloud', and l26 echoes s2e01 'Next! Token seven.' (the bible's English title is 'Token Seven'): the English s2e02 and s2e01 should match, or these lines follow them.

Tags: all kept from the Hindi, one per line, none stacked, no ellipsis straight after a tag, nothing whispered. l12 keeps the '!' inside [quietly]; give it extra takes as the Hindi note says. Verify-group tags as in the Hindi: [earnest] (l04, l14, l24), [deadpan] (l20), [smoothly] and [amused] (lawyer), [sharply] (l10, crisper not louder). The magistrate's English casting lines used [level] and the voice obeyed it in casting; [calm] is kept here to match the Hindi, and S10 may swap to [level].

Short turns: l08 'So you admit that—' is a deliberate cut-off; end it hard on the dash and start l09 with no gap. l26 (three words) and l25 (five) stand alone as in the Hindi; give l26 extra takes so 'one' is not swallowed under the music.

Timing estimate, not measured: targets were set by ear at about 2.3 to 2.6 words a second (about 12 characters a second), slower than the proof English targets, because Gate 0b measured real v4 takes 20 to 60 per cent over target. Spoken 97.6 s, 16 speaker changes at 0.3 s (4.8 s), silences 11.9 s (as the Hindi): 114.3 s, against the Hindi's 131.5 s (after the S5 review fix to l12, 5.8 to 5.0 s). About 1,198 characters of English dialogue, hand-counted without tags (English characters are not comparable with the Devanagari measure of D-016 direction 7). Nothing was padded to meet the Hindi length.

Lines more than about 15 per cent shorter than the Hindi target (English is denser than Hinglish here; the shots follow the measured voice under D-014 rule 6, so no padding): l03 6.0 against 7.6, l04 4.2/5.0, l08 1.5/2.0, l09 3.2/3.8, l10 3.8/4.6, l12 5.0/7.0, l17 5.6/6.9, l18 4.0/5.0, l19 2.3/2.8. None is short of its shot if the shots follow the voice; if S4 keeps the Hindi shot lengths for the English cut, b6 shot 4 and b9 shot 1 would hold about a second longer on the picture. l05 is the one line longer than the Hindi (3.8 against 3.5).

Not verified: the JSON has not been run through a parser (no shell in this session); the hi/en id, speaker and tag match was checked by eye, line by line, not by a tool; word and character counts and timings are by hand; no voice has spoken any English line in this file. The legal phrasing ('charges framed', 'bail rejected', 'stand trial') is ordinary Indian court English, not checked against any law.
